title: @object-ui/core: a compact notation option on formatMeasure, so chart axes and tables share one source for compact currency amounts
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYmRepQK9DkZeU7F53D

Filing gate: ② a fleet `Feature`, filed on the seat's ruling record · Source: fleet (ruling record 7153146695 on #37053: the maintainer ruled 「A」 for PR #37194's currency arm, and the record says option C becomes a follow-up card; filed by zone a4-U)

## What

`formatMeasure` in `@object-ui/core` (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/dataset-format.ts`) prints a measure the way a table cell shows it. For currency that means the full amount (`CN¥1,200,000.00`). It has no compact notation.

So PR #37194 (#37053) draws currency value-axis ticks through the chart's own compact formatter, `compactTickFormatter` with a `currency` argument, which prints `CN¥1.2M`. It takes the symbol from the same `Intl` source, but this is a second formatting home beside `formatMeasure`.

## Proposal

- Add a `notation` option (`'standard' | 'compact'`) to `formatMeasure`. With `compact`, it prints the amount through `Intl.NumberFormat`'s compact notation, keeping the measure's currency and percent rules.
- Then the chart's value-axis currency ticks call `formatMeasure(…, { notation: 'compact' })` instead of `compactTickFormatter`, so charts and tables share one compact source, as the ruling record says.
- A new option on an exported function: `Clause-②: yes` (widening).

## Acceptance

- `formatMeasure` with `notation: 'compact'` prints a fixed-ISO currency amount compactly with its symbol (en and zh-CN pinned). The default output is byte-identical to today.
- The chart's currency ticks route through it and match PR #37194's pinned readings (`CN¥0` … `CN¥12K`).

Blocked-by: #37194

Grading: area:ux · Feature · fleet source → p3, per the filing gate; triage to confirm.

Business reason: one formatting home for compact currency amounts keeps a report's chart axis and any future compact table cell in step, with no second implementation to drift. The ruling record names this as the follow-up.

Reader: the zone or seat that claims it after PR #37194 lands.

Dedupe: `formatMeasure notation` (open and closed) → 2 hits, #37053 (the parent) and #36988 (closed, the fraction-percent axis fix). Neither covers this option.
